conviction_note: Sum of four signed findings (+4.0 forwarding inflection, -1.5 domestic brokerage margin squeeze, +1.0 M&A posture, -0.5 CFO selling) = +3.0, deliberately set below the 5.65% historical median reaction because the two operating read-acrosses point in opposite directions and I could not obtain Radiant's air/ocean-versus-truck revenue split to weight them.

findings.finding: The global forwarding market inflected violently inside Radiant's fiscal Q4 (Apr-Jun 2026) and after Radiant last spoke: Expeditors went from +16% EPS / +5% air tonnage / +4% revenue in the March quarter (reported 2026-05-05) to +51% EPS / +14% tonnage / +57% airfreight revenue / +32% total revenue in the June quarter (reported 2026-08-03), driven by the 28-Feb Middle East escalation removing ~12% of global air cargo capacity and pushing air spot rates ~+40% y/y in May.
findings.why_not_priced: Radiant's own last word on international was 11 May 2026, when Crain described international as severely challenged by geopolitical disruption and tariffs, and the whole sell-side model is anchored there: the last analyst action on the name is Lake Street's $12 target dated 2026-06-08 with the stock at $8.88 — BEFORE both C.H. Robinson (07-29) and Expeditors (08-03) printed. If the market had marked Radiant to the June-quarter forwarding data the stock would be above its June level; instead it sits at $8.31, -4.6% over 20 days and 13.5% off its 52-week high, with put open interest 10.5x calls. The same stale-consensus mechanism produced adjusted EPS of $0.11 against a $0.043 consensus last quarter and a +9.76% print reaction, and +16.34% the quarter before.
findings.independence: Xeneta/Air Cargo News, a completely different source, dates the capacity shock and the rate spike to the same window: global spot rates ~+40% y/y in May 2026 and ~12% of global air cargo capacity removed on 28 February — https://www.aircargonews.net/data/2026/07/xeneta-rates-to-climb-by-up-to-15-in-2026-as-middle-east-conflict-weighs-in/ . Radiant's own history shows the gearing: Q4 FY2022 adjusted EBITDA was $27.7m in a rate-spike quarter against $7.9m in Q4 FY2025 — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171155/000095017022018408/rlgt-ex99_1.htm

findings.finding: The same June quarter crushed domestic truck-brokerage gross margin, which is the other half of Radiant's business: RXO's gross margin fell to 13.9% of revenue from 17.8%, and J.B. Hunt's brokerage purchased transportation rose 54% against 49% revenue growth, taking brokerage gross margin down 300bp to 12.5%, as truckload spot went to 42% of volume (+1,500bp y/y).
findings.why_not_priced: Radiant Road & Rail is a sub-scale broker with a contract book, and on 11 May Crain said he expected only 'high single-digit' increases on contract renewals while spot ran far above that — the classic sub-scale-broker squeeze. Nobody models Radiant's brokerage leg separately because the company collapsed its revenue disaggregation to two lines (Transportation Services / Value Added Services) in the Q3 10-Q, so a reader cannot see the truck exposure at all without the annual disclosure that arrives with tonight's 10-K. If this were priced, the peer-print period would have shown RLGT trading down with the small brokers rather than drifting.
findings.independence: Cass, an independent index, corroborates the mechanism in the same months: June 2026 expenditures +11.2% y/y against shipments -4.1% y/y, i.e. cost per shipment up roughly 16% — https://www.cassinfo.com/freight-audit-payment/cass-transportation-indexes/june-2026 . This finding deliberately cuts AGAINST finding 1 and is sized as a partial offset, not as independent confirmation of it.

findings.finding: Three post-Q3 corporate actions line up as a pending acquisition: the 7 Aug 2026 amended-and-restated credit agreement extends the $200m revolver to 2031 at lower spreads and raises the acquisition accordion from $75m to $100m; on 31 Aug Radiant hired David Buss, previously CEO of DB Schenker's North America cluster, as SVP/COO explicitly to 'manage diligence and integration efforts for ongoing acquisition initiatives'; and the buyback went to zero in the March quarter (585,050 shares bought in Q1+Q2 FY26, none in Q3) while cash built from $22.9m to $39.7m.
findings.why_not_priced: Each piece was released separately into a name with two to three covering analysts and 129k shares a day of volume, and the credit-facility release does not even appear on the company's own news page. Radiant has generated its last two years of EBITDA growth 'principally through our acquisition efforts' (FY2025 release), so a deal or a deal-shaped capital-allocation message on the call is the single most repriceable thing Crain can say — and if the market had connected the dots the stock would not have fallen ~6% since the COO announcement. The last note written on the name (2026-06-08) predates both 8-Ks.
findings.independence: Same thesis, different documents rather than independent confirmation — the COO 8-K is https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171155/000119312526382100/rlgt-20260831.htm (filed 2026-09-03) and the buyback/cash data is the Q3 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171155/000119312526216902/rlgt-20260331.htm (2026-05-11). Treat as one source cluster.

findings.finding: CFO Todd Macomber sold down to 87,249 shares by 15 June 2026, roughly halving his direct holding across sales at $7.00 (late March), ~$8.50 (27-28 May), $9.30 (9 June) and $9.25 (12-15 June) — i.e. he was a persistent seller right into fiscal year-end and every sale was above today's $8.31.
findings.why_not_priced: Only weakly unpriced — the individual Form 4s are aggregated by the usual trackers. What is not aggregated is the cumulative arc: four separate filings over eleven weeks that together halve the position, at prices the stock has not seen since. I size it small for exactly that reason; if it were fully priced the name would not still carry a Buy consensus and a $10.25 average target.

baseline_tension: It cuts against the tape: the baseline shows a stock that has drifted down (-4.6% over 20 days, -13.5% from its 52-week high) through exactly the six weeks in which its two largest listed peers reported the best forwarding quarter since 2022, and the only directional hint in the baseline — put open interest 10.5x calls — points the opposite way to my largest finding.
